scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After an upgrade attempt on r6, all routes for the r7 region
(67.0.0.0/8, 17.x.x.x, 70.0.0.0/8) became unreachable from
r1, even though r7 itself is still up and its ospfd is running.
What happened to the connectivity between r6 and the rest of
the backbone?
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r6 ospfd
Mechanism: r6 is the area 1 transit router connecting r7
  (and its 67.0.0.0/8, 17.x, 70.x) to the rest of area 1
  and onward to the backbone via r4. Without r6's ospfd,
  r7 has nobody to peer with — its routes never reach the
  backbone. From r1's perspective, all r7-region prefixes
  withdraw.
Localization: r6
Root cause: ospfd not running on r6
Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on r6

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r6" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The ospfd daemon on r6 is not running, even though it is enabled in
/etc/frr/daemons and a complete, valid configuration is present in
/etc/frr/frr.conf. The "upgrade attempt" on r6 killed the ospfd
process and it was never restarted; only zebra, mgmtd, and staticd
are alive on that router.

Because ospfd is dead, r6 forms no OSPF adjacencies on any of its
interfaces (eth0/S toward r4, eth1/V toward r5, eth2/Y toward r7,
eth3/Z stub). r7's sole link into the backbone runs through r6 on
segment Y (67.0.0.0/8). With no OSPF peer on that segment, r7 has
no OSPF neighbors at all and therefore cannot advertise its loopbacks
(17.1.x.1/32), its stub network (70.0.0.0/8), or the inter-router
link prefix (67.0.0.0/8) into the backbone. Equally, r6 no longer
distributes its own loopbacks (16.1.x.1) and stub (60.0.0.0/8) into
area 1. The backbone routers — including r1 — see every one of those
prefixes disappear from their OSPF LSDB, producing the observed
unreachability of the entire r7 region.

Root cause: ospfd was stopped on r6 during the upgrade and not
restarted, severing all OSPF adjacencies on r6 and isolating r7 from
the rest of the network.

Corrective fix: SSH to r6 and restart the FRR service to bring ospfd
back up — `service frr restart` (or `systemctl restart frr`). ospfd
will load /etc/frr/frr.conf, re-establish adjacencies with r4, r5,
and r7, and the missing routes will converge within a few OSPF hello
intervals.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly identifies r6 as the affected router where ospfd was stopped.
The agent explicitly identifies ospfd (the OSPF daemon) on r6 as stopped and the cause of the OSPF adjacency and route withdrawal issues.
The diagnosis explicitly blames ospfd being stopped on r6 (not a failure of r7), explains how that isolates r7, and prescribes restarting FRR on r6.
The agent recommends restarting the FRR/ospfd daemon on r6 (service frr restart or systemctl restart frr), which matches the expected fix to restore OSPF adjacencies.

The log contains direct evidence that ospfd is not running on r6 (vtysh/ps outputs), that /etc/frr/frr.conf contains OSPF configuration, and that r7 has no OSPF neighbors — supporting the conclusion that stopped ospfd on r6 caused the outage. The agent's attribution of the stop to an "upgrade attempt" is speculative and not shown in the logs.
